title: Tailoring H-mordenite to suppress coke formation and enhance selectivity in toluene alkylation with 1-heptene: a combined experimental and kinetic study
content: Linear alkylbenzenes are key precursors to linear alkylbenzene sulfonates, the world's most widely used anionic surfactants, with annual demand exceeding 3 Mt. Conventional industrial production relies on homogeneous acid catalysts such as HF and AlCl3, which present corrosion, safety, separation and waste-disposal challenges. Zeolites offer a regenerable heterogeneous alternative, but rapid coke-induced deactivation, particularly in narrow-pore structures such as mordenite. Here, the effect of framework modification on toluene alkylation with 1-heptene was investigated over H-mordenite, dealuminated H-mordenite and desilicated H-mordenite. Desilicated H-mordenite showed the best performance, achieving 97% 1-heptene conversion and 82% selectivity to 2-heptylmethylbenzene at a toluene-to-1-heptene ratio of 5 : 1, while also exhibiting improved resistance to coke deposition. Temperature-programmed oxidation and thermogravimetric analysis confirmed reduced carbon accumulation, while BET/BJH analysis, X-ray diffraction and FTIR spectroscopy showed that desilication generated substantial secondary mesoporosity while largely preserving the parent crystalline framework. The experimental results were further described using a kinetic model comprising seven species and thirteen elementary pathways. Kinetic parameters were estimated by nonlinear optimisation using a genetic algorithm, with the resulting differential equations solved using a fourth-order Runge–Kutta method. The derived activation energies indicated generally lower barriers for isomerisation (29.4–78.8 kJ mol−1) and toluene alkylation (41.5–94.9 kJ mol−1) than for coke-forming pathways, particularly direct olefin oligomerisation and dimerisation (142.4–202.3 kJ mol−1). This integrated experimental-modelling approach establishes a strategy for improving diffusion, catalyst lifetime and process efficiency under industrially relevant conditions for more efficient linear alkylbenzene production under industrially relevant conditions.
